concepts.label: StaffId
concepts.definition: The enterprise-wide staff number issued by the HR system and used as the internal primary key by older enterprise systems. Exactly 7 characters: U or N followed by 6 digits, case-insensitive and normalised to uppercase. Unique per member of staff, never reissued and never changed. The identity provider is its source of truth; applications read it from a token claim and do not edit it.

concepts.label: AcceptProposal
concepts.definition: Creates or updates the calling Manager's own `ProposalAcceptance`; on the 3rd acceptance, atomically creates the `ConfirmedSlot` and its `SlotCapacity` rows.

concepts.label: ActorType
concepts.definition: Who caused an audited change: an Entra ID staff identity, a candidate acting through a tokenised link, or a background job.

concepts.label: AdjustConfirmedSlotCapacity
concepts.definition: Lets a Manager replace `totalHeadcount` on the `SlotCapacity` for their current `AppointmentType`, changing `remainingCapacity` by the same delta while holding the same row lock used by `AdjustSlotCapacity`.

concepts.label: AdjustSlotCapacity
concepts.definition: The row-locked read-check-write path for booking-driven changes to `SlotCapacity.remainingCapacity`.

concepts.label: AppointmentType
concepts.definition: One of the 3 fixed appointment types (Drug & Alcohol Testing, Medical Check-up, Uniform Fitting). `code` is the short form (`DAT`, `MED`, `UNI`) used as the `ConfirmedSlot` CSV import column headers; a `Candidate`'s required `AppointmentType`s are derived from `EmployeeGroupRequirement` via the `Candidate`'s `EmployeeGroup` and are no longer selected directly by candidate CSV upload. Under the scoped multi-role design, its current Manager is derived from the unique Manager `StaffAccessProfile` rather than duplicated on this entity.

concepts.label: AuditAction
concepts.definition: The complete set of state changes recorded in `AuditLog`, including candidate Employee Group assignments, recovery lifecycle actions, access-profile actions, and appointment-delivery actions. `StaffRolesSynced` records an identity-provider-driven role change with `ActorType.System`, distinct from the Admin-driven `StaffAccessChanged`/`StaffAccessRemoved` scope actions. Candidate and appointment details contain identifiers, canonical codes, and old/new statuses only, never names, email addresses, clinical data, or arbitrary free text.

concepts.label: AuditLog
concepts.definition: An append-only record of a state change to `SlotProposal`, `ConfirmedSlot`, `Candidate`, `Invite`, `Booking`, `StaffAccessProfile`, or `BookingAppointment`. Candidate group changes and recovery actions store fixed identifiers, canonical codes, and statuses only. A candidate-scoped history covers the entries recorded against the `Candidate` record itself and against their `Invite`, `Booking`, and `BookingAppointment` records.

concepts.label: Booking
concepts.definition: Created when a `Candidate` confirms one `InviteOption`. `inviteId` records which `Invite` it came from. `recoveryOfBookingId` is null for the original shared-slot Booking and identifies that original Booking for a later missed-appointment recovery. A recovery Booking may become `Concluded`; cancellation sets `status` rather than deleting the row so history survives.

concepts.label: BookingAppointment
concepts.definition: The operational instance of one required `AppointmentType` within one `Booking`. It progresses independently through check-in and outcome states, records the latest staff changer, and is unique per (`Booking`, `AppointmentType`) pair.

concepts.label: BookingAppointmentStatus
concepts.definition: Independent operational progress for one `BookingAppointment`. Normal progress is `Expected` → `CheckedIn` → `Completed`, with `Expected` → `NoShow` as the alternative outcome and bounded one-step corrections back toward `Expected`.

concepts.label: BookingStatus
concepts.definition: An `Active` original Booking is the Candidate's appointment journey root. An active recovery Booking holds its own `SlotCapacity`; it becomes `Concluded` once every one of its Booking Appointments has reached `Completed` or `NoShow`, preserving history while allowing another recovery after a no-show.

concepts.label: Candidate
concepts.definition: A person invited to attend appointments, entered via CSV upload or CRUD API. `employeeGroupId` is nullable only during the staged legacy reconciliation window and required for every new Candidate. `statusChangedAt` is stamped by the persistence layer whenever `status` is written, and is what the coordinator dashboards mean by "waiting since".

concepts.label: CandidateReadiness
concepts.definition: A calculated, non-persisted view of whether the current derived requirements are satisfied across the active original Booking and its non-cancelled recovery Bookings. It contains only a stable reason code plus outstanding Appointment Type codes and names.

concepts.label: CandidateReadinessCode
concepts.definition: Stable internal reason describing the Candidate's appointment readiness. Only `Ready` means every current derived requirement has a Completed Booking Appointment in the non-cancelled booking journey.

concepts.label: CandidateRequirement
concepts.definition: One materialized `AppointmentType` a given `Candidate` currently requires, derived only from that Candidate's active `EmployeeGroup`. Legacy rows remain unchanged until explicit reconciliation.

concepts.label: CandidateStatus
concepts.definition: Where a `Candidate` sits in the invite/booking lifecycle. Surfaced verbatim (with friendlier wording) on the coordinator dashboards.

concepts.label: ConfirmedSlot
concepts.definition: A `SlotProposal` accepted by all 3 managers, or a slot an Admin or Coordinator bulk-imported directly; bookable by candidates either way. `proposalId` is null for an imported slot — that nullability is its provenance marker, no separate field needed. `date` and `startTime` are carried as one `SlotWindow`.

concepts.label: ConfirmedSlotStatus
concepts.definition: `Active` slots are the only ones an `Invite` may offer.

concepts.label: EmailLog
concepts.definition: A durable record of one candidate email delivery attempt. Identity, template, and safe context identifiers are immutable; claim and outcome fields transition from `Pending` to `Sent`, `Failed`, or `Resolved`. The nullable context identifiers regenerate a message without storing raw tokens, URLs, or bodies.

concepts.label: EmailStatus
concepts.definition: Outcome of one `EmailLog` delivery attempt. `Pending` means the business transaction committed and dispatch has not yet reached a terminal provider outcome; `Failed` remains the failed-email count; `Resolved` means a later durable retry superseded an outstanding attempt.

concepts.label: EmailTemplate
concepts.definition: The 4 candidate-facing emails.

concepts.label: EmployeeGroup
concepts.definition: Change-controlled reference data describing one employment category. Its immutable canonical `code` identifies it at import and MCP boundaries; its mappings determine the current `CandidateRequirement` set. The first release contains Cabin Crew (`CABIN_CREW`), Pilots (`PILOTS`), Ground Operations Agent (`GROUND_OPERATIONS_AGENT`), Engineering (`ENGINEERING`), and Ground Transport Services (`GROUND_TRANSPORT_SERVICES`) only.

concepts.label: EmployeeGroupRequirement
concepts.definition: One fixed `AppointmentType` required by an `EmployeeGroup`. The complete mapping is seeded once as reviewed reference data rather than duplicated in handlers or clients.

concepts.label: ImportConfirmedSlots
concepts.definition: Validates a CSV of already-agreed slots for an Admin or Coordinator and, all-or-nothing, creates each row's `ConfirmedSlot` and its 3 `SlotCapacity` rows directly — bypassing `ProposeSlot`/`AcceptProposal` entirely.

concepts.label: Invite
concepts.definition: An offer to a `Candidate` of 3 `ConfirmedSlot` options, carrying a single-use signed token and a snapshotted requirement set. `recoveryOfBookingId` is null for an initial booking invitation and identifies the active original `Booking` for missed-appointment recovery.

concepts.label: InviteOption
concepts.definition: One of the 3 `ConfirmedSlot` options offered within an `Invite`.

concepts.label: InviteRequirement
concepts.definition: One `AppointmentType` snapshotted when an `Invite` is issued. An initial Invite snapshots all current derived `CandidateRequirement` rows; a recovery Invite snapshots only still-outstanding no-show types.

concepts.label: InviteStatus
concepts.definition: `Used` once a `Booking` is made against it; `Expired` once the sweep passes its `expiresAt`; `Superseded` when a newer Invite or a changed Employee Group replaces it; `Cancelled` when a Coordinator explicitly ends a recovery Invite.

concepts.label: OutstandingAppointmentType
concepts.definition: Minimum-data readiness detail for one current Candidate Requirement that has no Completed Booking Appointment in the non-cancelled booking journey. `isRecoverable` is true only when its latest non-cancelled attempt is No-show.

concepts.label: ProposalAcceptance
concepts.definition: One manager's acceptance of a `SlotProposal`, carrying their own headcount. The same manager may revise `headcount` in place while the proposal remains `Open`; another manager may not read or change it.

concepts.label: ProposeSlot
concepts.definition: Creates a `SlotProposal` with status Open.

concepts.label: ReassignAppointmentTypeManager
concepts.definition: Atomically changes which `StaffAccessProfile` holds Manager for an `AppointmentType`, preserving the former profile's other roles.

concepts.label: ReplaceStaffAccessProfile
concepts.definition: Superseded by `ReplaceStaffAccessProfileScope`. Previously created or atomically replaced one identity's complete role set, shared appointment-type scope, and concurrency version while enforcing Admin exclusivity and Manager uniqueness; role assignment is no longer an Admin-driven operation. The name remains canonical only so the Issue #71 design and narrative continue to describe the implementation they recorded accurately.

concepts.label: ReplaceStaffAccessProfileScope
concepts.definition: Atomically replaces an existing `StaffAccessProfile`'s `appointmentTypeId` scope and concurrency version, enforcing Manager uniqueness per `AppointmentType`. Cannot create a profile or change `roles`; targets only a `staffUserId` that already has a profile from its own role sync.

concepts.label: RetryEmail
concepts.definition: Locks the newest unresolved `EmailLog` for a `Candidate`, derives its `EmailTemplate` and safe context server-side, rotates any token hash, and stages a fresh attempt before post-commit dispatch.

concepts.label: Role
concepts.definition: The identity-provider-assigned staff roles (Entra App Roles in production, Keycloak realm roles in local/dev), mirrored onto `StaffAccessProfile` rather than administered by JointBooking. Admin is exclusive; Coordinator is unscoped and may combine with Manager and/or AppointmentStaff; Manager and AppointmentStaff use the profile's single `AppointmentType` scope. `Candidate` is deliberately not a `Role` value — candidates are token-authenticated, not staff identities.

concepts.label: SlotCapacity
concepts.definition: Remaining bookable headcount for one `AppointmentType` on one `ConfirmedSlot`. While the slot is `Active`, its current Manager may replace `totalHeadcount` with a positive total that covers every active booking requiring that type; `remainingCapacity` changes by the same delta.

concepts.label: SlotProposal
concepts.definition: A candidate-facing 4-hour window proposed by one manager; other managers accept it independently. `date` and `startTime` are carried as one `SlotWindow`.

concepts.label: SlotProposalStatus
concepts.definition: `Open` until every `AppointmentType` has a `ProposalAcceptance`; `Confirmed` once a `ConfirmedSlot` has been derived from it; `Withdrawn` if a scoped `Manager` or `Admin` pulls it before that.

concepts.label: SlotWindow
concepts.definition: The 4-hour candidate-facing window shared by `SlotProposal` and `ConfirmedSlot`. Duration is fixed at 4 hours, so the end time is derived, never stored. Persisted into the owning row's own `date` and `startTime` columns rather than a table of its own.

concepts.label: StaffAccessProfile
concepts.definition: The application's mirror of one authenticated staff identity's access: `roles` is written only by JointBooking's own identity-provider-claims sync and is never administered directly, while `appointmentTypeId` and `version` remain fully Admin-owned. Admin is exclusive and unscoped; Coordinator may combine with Manager and/or AppointmentStaff; Manager and AppointmentStaff share one `AppointmentType` scope, which may briefly be null immediately after a scoped role is synced and before an Admin assigns it — that transitional shape grants no capabilities. Absence of a profile means the authenticated identity is unassigned.

concepts.label: StaffCapability
concepts.definition: The named permissions `StaffAccessAuthorizer` checks a `StaffAccessProfile`'s `roles` against, pinning down the "capability" vocabulary the Issue #71 design describes only in prose (its role/capability table). Every staff-facing handler requests one of these rather than checking `Role` directly, so a newly added role gains only the capabilities its role mapping grants.

concepts.label: StaffId
concepts.definition: The enterprise-wide staff number issued by the HR system and used as the internal primary key by older enterprise systems. Exactly 7 characters: `U` or `N` followed by 6 digits, case-insensitive — always normalised to uppercase, so two values differing only in case are the same `StaffId`. Unique per member of staff, never reissued and never changed, which is what makes it safe for JointBooking to mirror. The identity provider is its source of truth; JointBooking only ever reads it from a token claim and never edits it.

concepts.label: StaffIdentity
concepts.definition: The application's mirror of one authenticated staff identity: the provider-assigned `staffUserId` paired with the `StaffId` that identity's token carries, learned from the token itself. It exists so an Admin can address a colleague by `StaffId` instead of by opaque identifier, and so `StaffId` can be shown wherever a staff identity is displayed. `displayName` is the same idea applied to a human-readable name rather than the staff number, mirrored from the token's own name claim when the identity provider is configured to emit one; it is null when no such claim has ever been observed for that identity. It is a cache of identity-provider-owned data and is never the source of truth for any field. A row appears the first time an identity calls the API, which may be before any `StaffAccessProfile` assigns it a role.

concepts.label: SyncStaffAccessProfileRoles
concepts.definition: Reads the caller's identity-provider `roles` claim during `GET /api/me`, upserts `StaffAccessProfile.roles` only when it differs from the persisted value, clears dependent `appointmentTypeId` scope when no scoped role remains, and rejects (without overwriting) a syntactically valid but semantically invalid role combination. Not reachable through any Admin-facing route.

concepts.label: SystemSettings
concepts.definition: Single-row Admin-configurable settings.

concepts.label: UpdateSystemSettings
concepts.definition: Validates and persists `SystemSettings` (invite expiry window, max auto-retry count).

concepts.label: UserRoleAssignment
concepts.definition: Removed legacy single-role entity superseded by `StaffAccessProfile` in Issue #71. The name remains canonical only so accepted historical plans and narrative continue to describe the implementation they recorded accurately.

concepts.label: VoidBooking
concepts.definition: Increments `SlotCapacity` (via `AdjustSlotCapacity`), voids a `Booking`, and resets the `Candidate`'s status to "Not yet invited". Shared by both cancellation paths.

concepts.label: WithdrawAcceptance
concepts.definition: Removes a Manager's own `ProposalAcceptance`, only while the `SlotProposal` has fewer than 3 acceptances.

concepts.label: WithdrawProposal
concepts.definition: Sets a `SlotProposal`'s status to Withdrawn (creator only, pre-confirmation).

concepts.label: scopes Manager and AppointmentStaff roles for

relations.label: scopes Manager and AppointmentStaff roles for

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_1
rules.label: `StaffAccessProfile`
rules.text: Admin is exclusive and has no `AppointmentType`; Coordinator may combine with Manager and/or AppointmentStaff but never Admin; Manager and AppointmentStaff share the profile's one `AppointmentType` scope. Admin receives no candidate data. Each `AppointmentType` has at most one current Manager profile, while any number of AppointmentStaff profiles may share it. Manager or AppointmentStaff may transiently carry a null scope immediately after an identity-provider role sync and before an Admin assigns the appointment type; that shape is valid but grants no capabilities until scope is set. See [Issue #71 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-scoped-multi-role-authorization-design.md) and [IdP-sourced roles design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-idp-sourced-staff-roles-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_10
rules.label: `CandidateReadiness`
rules.text: `Ready` requires an active original Booking and one Completed Booking Appointment for every current derived Candidate Requirement across that original Booking and its non-cancelled recovery Bookings. Expected, Checked in, and No-show are outstanding; cancelled Booking Appointments and non-required Appointment Types are excluded. No active original Booking, a temporarily unassigned Employee Group, or a requirement snapshot mismatch is explicitly not ready. See [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_11
rules.label: Recovery Booking
rules.text: A recovery Invite and Booking cover only current requirements whose latest non-cancelled Booking Appointment is No-show and for which no Completed attempt exists. Completed appointments are never recreated or charged capacity again. A recovery Booking becomes Concluded when all its appointments are Completed or No-show; repeated No-show can then create another recovery. A No-show correction is rejected while a later pending or non-cancelled recovery exists. See [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_12
rules.label: `SlotWindow`
rules.text: Every window is exactly 4 hours; only its `date` and `startTime` are stored, so a proposal and the `ConfirmedSlot` derived from it can never disagree about duration. See [Plan 02](detailed-implementations/2026-09-03-joint-booking/02-domain-appointment-types.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_13
rules.label: `StaffIdentity`
rules.text: Exactly one row per authenticated staff identity, keyed by `staffUserId`, with `staffId` unique across the table. Both fields are immutable in practice: the provider never reissues `staffUserId` for the same person and HR never changes a `StaffId`. An authenticated request whose pair is not already cached upserts it, so the mirror converges from tokens alone, without a directory query; `lastSeenAt` is refreshed on those writes only and is therefore approximate. `displayName` refreshes on the same cache-miss cadence as `lastSeenAt` and carries the same approximateness — it can lag a rename in the identity provider until the next sign-in — and, unlike `staffId`, its absence never blocks anything: a null `displayName` falls back to `staffId` or an opaque identifier wherever a staff identity is shown. A token with no `StaffId` claim, or one carrying a malformed value, records no row and is refused by every staff-authorized endpoint even where a `StaffAccessProfile` exists, since a staff identity JointBooking cannot name must not appear in an `AuditLog`. See [StaffId claim design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-staff-id-claim-design.md) and [Staff identity display name design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-staff-identity-display-name-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_2
rules.label: `ConfirmedSlot`
rules.text: A `SlotProposal` becomes a `ConfirmedSlot` only once all 3 Managers (one per `AppointmentType`) have accepted it, each supplying their own headcount. An Admin or Coordinator may instead bulk-import a `ConfirmedSlot` directly, with `proposalId` left null; either way, once created it behaves identically for every later operation. See [Area B](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/b-slot-negotiation.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_3
rules.label: `ProposalAcceptance`
rules.text: While its `SlotProposal` remains `Open`, the manager recorded in `managerUserId` may replace their own positive `headcount` without withdrawing the acceptance. A different manager cannot read or change that value. See [Area B](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/b-slot-negotiation.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_4
rules.label: `SlotCapacity`
rules.text: `remainingCapacity` must never go below 0 or above the current `totalHeadcount` for that `AppointmentType` on that `ConfirmedSlot`. While the slot remains `Active`, its current Manager may replace `totalHeadcount` with a positive total no lower than the active-booking count, changing `remainingCapacity` by the same delta. Every read-check-write is one atomic, row-locked transaction. This is the mechanism behind "no overbooking." See [Area G](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/g-capacity-concurrency-rules.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_5
rules.label: `Invite`
rules.text: Every `Invite` offers exactly 3 `InviteOption`s, each a `ConfirmedSlot` with spare `SlotCapacity` in every snapshotted `InviteRequirement`. An initial Invite snapshots every current derived `CandidateRequirement`; a recovery Invite snapshots only recoverable outstanding no-show types and identifies the active original Booking. A group-changing edit supersedes a pending initial Invite, while a Coordinator may explicitly cancel a recovery Invite. See [Area D](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/d-invite-engine.md) and [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_6
rules.label: `Booking`
rules.text: Cancelling a `ConfirmedSlot` voids every `Booking` against it, frees its `SlotCapacity`, and triggers a fresh `Invite` for each affected `Candidate`. See [Area F](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/f-cancellation-reschedule.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_7
rules.label: `BookingAppointment`
rules.text: A booking creates exactly one per candidate requirement in the same transaction, unique by (`Booking`, `AppointmentType`). Its normal lifecycle is `Expected` → `CheckedIn` → `Completed` or `Expected` → `NoShow`; only the bounded corrections `CheckedIn` → `Expected`, `Completed` → `CheckedIn`, and `NoShow` → `Expected` are permitted. A same-status submission is idempotent. Check-in is limited to the slot's head-office date, no-show is permitted only after its four-hour window, and every real transition is versioned and audited. Active bookings and active slots are required for mutation. See [Issue #26 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-booking-appointment-workspace-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_8
rules.label: `CandidateRequirement`
rules.text: The requirement set cannot change while the candidate has an active original `Booking`; name and email corrections and set-equivalent Employee Group changes remain permitted. Outside a legacy reconciliation window, requirements are derived only from the Candidate's active `EmployeeGroup` and are never caller-selected. Cancellation makes old `BookingAppointment` records read-only and a replacement initial booking snapshots the then-current set. See [Issue #26 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-booking-appointment-workspace-design.md) and [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md).

rules.subject: https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#_invariant_9
rules.label: `EmployeeGroup`
rules.text: The initial five groups and their mappings to the existing three fixed Appointment Types are deterministic, change-controlled reference data. Every active group has at least one known, non-duplicated mapping. Group codes are immutable, unique, canonical uppercase snake case, and accepted case-insensitively at input boundaries. Runtime editing and dynamic Appointment Types are outside Issue #91. See [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md).
